title: Data Freshness Before Entry
youtube_title: Data Freshness Before Entry: Why Stale Evidence Can Mislead
youtube_description: A paper-trading process is only as reliable as the evidence behind it. This short explains why timestamps, completed bars, quote freshness and market scope should be checked before treating a setup as eligible. Paper-trading education only; not live-money performance; not investment advice; no guaranteed returns.

improvement: Compared with the previous three vertical releases, this short makes the hook timestamp-driven in the first scene and uses a clearer evidence chain from time -> completed bar -> quote freshness -> market scope before the stand-down conclusion.

scenes.title: Start with the timestamp
scenes.narration: A chart can look precise while the evidence behind it is already stale. Start by checking when the data was created.

scenes.title: Use completed bars
scenes.narration: Use completed, timestamped bars for the decision. An unfinished candle can change its shape before the session is over.

scenes.title: Know the source
scenes.narration: Confirm the data source and market scope. The same symbol can be quoted differently across routes and feeds.

scenes.title: Look for missing pieces
scenes.narration: Missing history, stale quotes or material gaps can make a setup look stronger than the evidence actually supports.

scenes.title: Require fresh confirmation
scenes.narration: Only after freshness and intraday confirmation are checked should a setup be treated as eligible for further review.

scenes.title: Pause when unclear
scenes.narration: If the evidence chain cannot be verified, standing down is the disciplined result. A process does not need a trade every day.
